title.full: Global energy and climate outlook 2024 – Updating NDCs and closing the ambition gap – Indicators for 1.5°C alignment

description: Global model extrapolating trends under currently legislated policies.

coreDrivers.policies: The pathway is aligned with current and legislated policies: the pathway includes policies legislated as of June 2024 with no additional pledged targets.
coreDrivers.emissionsTargets: Legislated policies drive emissions forecast; resulting a pathway with a 2.6°C end-century warming.
coreDrivers.technologyCosts: Technology learning are endogenously developed in POLES-JRC; cost trend decreases as much as the technology is being adopted.
coreDrivers.investmentChange: Annual power-sector investment increases by 40% through 2050, with wind and solar accounting for around two-thirds of total investment, while fossil-fuel power investment remains material. However, GDP doubles over the same period, meaning that power-sector investment declines as a share of GDP.
coreDrivers.macroeconomicDrivers: Population and GDP assumptions are shared across the GECO scenarios and set the activity baseline. Inputs combine World Bank, IMF, OECD/SSP2, EU Ageing Report and JRC-IIASA sources.

dependencies.dependency_description: Legislated power policies drive the mix with exogenous capacity additions and technology mix inputs, but they do not require full decarbonisation and the pathway remains exposed to fossil fuel.

The GEM-E3 Social Accounting Matrix supports assessment of the Market & economics dependency by quantifying sectoral input–output relationships and international trade flows, allowing the pathway analysis to identify how each sector depends on upstream markets, production costs and imported inputs.

Renewables penetration is lower in this scenario, as fossil fuel power plants remains active. This means lower demand on grid flexibility and lower constraint on transmission lines. This is not detailed in the report.

Wind, solar and other renewables are associated with potentials and supply curves per country. This scenario depends on country legislated plan, and ressource availability will only be an indirect barrier.
Low: renewable-power employment grows in the Reference pathway, implying some workforce expansion, but GECO does not identify shortages, skills bottlenecks or higher unemployment.
Existing policy context is included but no deep aviation decarbonisation constraint is imposed. Any industry related targets is not included in the scenario.

The GEM-E3 Social Accounting Matrix supports assessment of the Market & economics dependency by quantifying sectoral input–output relationships and international trade flows, allowing the pathway analysis to identify how each sector depends on upstream markets, production costs and imported inputs.
Sustainable-fuel supply logistics are not defined as a bottleneck constraint in Reference.
